claims.evidence: PRIDE instruments = Q Exactive HF (MS:1002523); paper Methods "detected on an Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer"; every sampled raw header (one per MaxQuant search) reads "Q Exactive HF - Orbitrap MS". MS:1002523 label verified in OLS.
Paper: "analyzed on a Q Exactive HF ... using data-dependent acquisition"; raw method headers: "FULL MS / DD-MS2 (TOPN)". PRIDE:0000627 verified in OLS.
Raw method headers give "(N)CE / stepped (N)CE nce: 27/30" in dd-MS2 on the Q Exactive HF, whose only MS2 activation is HCD (beam-type CID). MS:1000422 verified in OLS.
dd-MS2 scans acquired at Orbitrap resolution 15,000 (HA-IP, N2a AS_146) / 30,000 (diGly, N2a AS204) per raw method header; MaxQuant FTMS MS/MS tolerance applies. MS:1000484 verified in OLS.

mqpar.xml of every search: <mainSearchTol>4.5</mainSearchTol>, <searchTolInPpm>true</searchTolInPpm> (first search 20 ppm). Note: the paper text says "main search peptide mass tolerance 0.5 D", which matches the ITMS MS/MS tolerance in mqpar, not the precursor setting; the deposited mqpar.xml is taken as authoritative.
mqpar.xml msmsParams Name="FTMS" MatchTolerance 20, MatchToleranceInPpm true; MS2 spectra are Orbitrap (FTMS) per raw headers.

Paper/PRIDE: "trypsinized" (IP), "trypsinization overnight" (APEX2), "Subsequent digestion of peptides with trypsin (Promega)" (diGly). MaxQuant enzyme Trypsin/P (search rule; recorded as note, batch rule 2). MS:1001251 verified in OLS.

diGly protocol (paper and PRIDE): "lysates were digested with 5 ng/ul lys-C (Wako) for 1 h at RT. Subsequent digestion of peptides with trypsin". MS:1001309 verified in OLS. Column inserted by the deterministic post-build step scripts/postbuild.py --lysc (batch rule 2).
diGly: "After reduction with 5 mM DTT and alkylation with 10 mM chloroacetamide". PRIDE:0000608 verified in OLS.
diGly: "alkylation with 10 mM chloroacetamide". PRIDE:0000600 verified in OLS.

limitations: Deposit is mixed: 48 SILAC (K0/K8) diGly runs and 24 label-free HA-IP / APEX2 runs; split by labelling and organism into PXD030729-digly-human, -digly-mouse, -lfq-human, -lfq-mouse (batch rule 12). All 72 deposited .raw files are annotated; none is left out.

The two sequential anti-diGly IPs of each SILAC mixture are encoded as comment[fraction identifier] 1 and 2 of one sample (MaxQuant gives both raw files the same Experiment name and sums them). Which raw file is the first and which the second IP is not stated anywhere; fraction 1 is assigned to the earlier acquisition (lower AS run number, the first block of four runs), an ordering inference.

comment[collision energy] and comment[ms1 scan range] are omitted: only one raw header per MaxQuant search was range-read and the values differ between searches (NCE 27 HA-IP vs 30 diGly; MS1 300-1650 vs 300-1750 m/z), so per-file values were not verified.

The paper states main search tolerance "0.5 D" and a human UniProt database for all diGly searches; the deposited mqpar.xml files give 4.5 ppm main-search precursor tolerance (0.5 Da is the ITMS MS/MS tolerance) and a mouse UP000000589 FASTA for the N2a searches. The mqpar.xml is followed.
No CCNF peptide was identified in the diGly-enriched N2a data, so the knockout channel could not be checked directly on CCNF; the directional check uses the paper-reported Map1b/Peg10 sites.
Developmental stage and passage number not reported: not available.
